name: Prayer, praise & worship
about: How to pray, vows, and praise.

teachings.title: Seek His face in prayer
teachings.summary: As David modeled, believers are commanded to seek God's face in faith and prayer, confessing sin and trusting His faithfulness and deliverance through trouble.
teachings.text:
Continuing Psalm 27, after establishing the faith on which he stands, and the confidence he has on the promises of God, David as psalmist cries out to the Lord for His mercy, to hear his prayer.

As these are meant to be sung or said, as model prayers or devotional worship, we are called to do the same. To call upon the mercy of the Lord. To bless His longsuffering and grace towards us, and petition the Lord with prayer.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

When we seek the Lord, it is obedience to His command to seek His face. To search for Him. As individuals and as a nation of believers.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

*Seek and ye shall find*, the Bible says. Our God is merciful to hear our prayers and to reward those that in faith, have sought Him out. What a humbling and amazing thing to be considered worthy of attention by our Creator.

David continues, meekly asking for forgiveness if there are any transgressions that may have displeased the Lord. Asking for His favor, to not forsake us in times of trouble, yet having the understanding that our trouble may be due to our own unresolved sin. Either way, *O God of* our *salvation,* hear our prayers.

In the very next breath, David affirms the steadfast faithfulness of the Lord, that even if our own parents forsake us, He remains true.

Expressing fear and doubt while recognizing the truth of the promises of God is a human thing, and we see this play out on our own minds, even as it does David's. We are a weak and needy people, and we need God involved in every aspect of our lives.

Remember this, and be open to His teaching. Be open to hearing His voice in scripture, recognizing the chastening in our life, seeing His mercy towards us, and wrath revealed from Heaven, and fearing Him, always.

He shows us the path. He gives us a way out of every temptation.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

We may ask for His help to see the deliverance He has for us, even as our adversaries seek to destroy us with their lies and schemes.

*I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.*

The evidence of God's grace and mercy to His people gives us faith and strength to carry on. This is a key reason why it is important to praise Him in the congregation, to edify those going through the trials of life, to have hope. That all things work together for good. To wait, patiently for the Lord to move. To be of good courage, knowing what He as done for others and has done for us in the past. Knowing our present suffering leads to the glory we are partakers in, through Christ.

**Romans 8:35–37**
*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

Amen

teachings.title: Importunity and imprecatory prayer are Biblical
teachings.summary: Persistent prayer and imprecatory prayer, as in the parable of the widow, are Biblical and powerful tools of faith, against teachers who say otherwise.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 17** again shows us the model of importunity in prayer.

Importunity is a noun that means asking for something over and over again in a strong, pushy, or annoying way. It is the act of persistent begging or making urgent demands that wear people down. David utilizes this in Psalms to great effect. Pursuing an answer from the throne of God, with repeated supplication.

It may seem contrary to the fear of the Lord and humility before Him, but scripture shows it is effective. Jesus taught us this as well.

**Luke 18:1–8**
*And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint; Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary. And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man; Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me. And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith. And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them? I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?*

We often find ourselves in difficult situations, where we have not because we ask not. We also tend to move on, rather than "bother God" with whatever it is we need of Him.

Praying without ceasing, staying strong in prayer because we are weak, this is pleasing to the Lord. So we should pray without fainting, and in doing so, exercise our faith that should Christ return in our time, He finds that faith upon the earth.

Notice too, that the woman before the unjust judge is pleading for vengeance against her adversary, just as David is here in this psalm. Just as the martyred under the throne in Heaven plead with God for His wrath to pour out.

Imprecatory prayers are Biblical. Acknowledging God's ownership of vengeance, while suffering for His sake, is an act of great faith. And as we have seen previously in **Psalms,** patience is a virtue that leads us to godliness.

Importunity in prayer, and imprecatory prayer feels wrong to many. I have seen supposed Christian teachers make the claim that there is no room for this in the New Testament. But they are a mighty tool in our arsenal of faith.

teachings.title: My grace is sufficient for thee
teachings.summary: An unanswered prayer may be answered by God's sufficient grace; remembering how He already delivered us keeps us from complaining like Israel in the wilderness.
teachings.text:
**2 Corinthians 12:7–11**
*And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong. I am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I be nothing.*

It's also good to remember that, if a prayer remains "unanswered" by our measure, it very well may be answered in His. That His grace is sufficient. We've already been spared, hell and deaf, and given the glory of eternal life in Christ.

Remember the Israelites, who when delivered out of Egypt and bondage, complained incessantly in the wilderness. They complained about a lack of water. They complained about the daunting task of taking the land, despite God promising to drive the inhabitants out before them. They believed the bad spies report, and ignored Joshua and Caleb. They complained about mana, and they complained about quail. And God had to constantly remind them that He had delivered them in the first place.

Sometimes if we feel the need to complain to God, we should remember that he's delivered us in the first place. That His grace is sufficient. Reminding ourselves of what we're going through currently is nothing in comparison to the abundance we've already received.

**Romans 8:14–18**
*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

Keeping that eternal perspective gives us faith in the Lord's of ability to deliver us. The suffering of this present time is nothing. Life is but a vapor.

So, having persistent prayer and letting God know how you feel while waiting for His perfect timing to occur is fine. But keep that perspective in mind. And understand that patience builds godliness. And everything to His glory, amen.

teachings.title: Persistent prayer like the importunate widow
teachings.summary: Scripture and Christ's parable of the widow teach persistent prayer for a matter while accepting His will, and gratitude for His answer often brings greater blessing.
teachings.text:
One of the effective means of prayer taught in Psalms, and reinforced by Jesus, is importunity. Persistent prayer. David will frequently ask the Lord to deliver his enemies and ask how long must he suffer the affliction in his life. There is nothing wrong with persistently going to God and asking for His resolution to the matter to come quickly.

**Luke 18:1–8**
*And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint; Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary. And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man; Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me. And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith. And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them? I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?*

We should not be afraid to bother the Lord with long-standing issues, be it health, or work, or enemies or anything else. Praying for resolution of a matter, while understanding that His will be done, and resigning yourself for whatever the end of the matter is, is crucial in the Christian prayer life.

And often, settling it in your heart to be glad with whatever God has given you in terms of an answer will lead to Him blessing you with yet a better alternative or outcome.

I have personally experienced this. I have witnessed it in others. Persistent prayer and genuine gratitude for whatever His will is, can often work miracles and bring the Lord to not only give you mercy, but shower you with His grace.

teachings.title: Seek first, not divination
teachings.summary: Consulting anything but God may bring a false answer that serves His purpose to our hurt, so start with His word and prayer, content with His will.
teachings.text:
It is interesting to note that the Babylonians were at the crossroads between Judah and Amon, and we're using divination, the reading of organs like the liver of an animal, to determine which way to go. God says he would give them a false divination, that they do His will.

When we have a decision to make, and we consult any other source but God, understand that He may well give you a false divination, allow bad advice or words that tickles your itching ear, to give you what you want, and plenty of it. Or to be used for His purpose, but your own destruction.

Seek ye first the Kingdom of God. Start in His word and in prayer. Delight yourself in the word of the Lord. Know His ways. Then enter into prayer, understanding that His grace is sufficient. Content with whatever His will may be.

Then will He give you what you need. It may not be what your heart wants, but it will be what serves Him.

teachings.title: I will not be enquired of by you
teachings.summary: God will not be enquired of by those whose hearts are not right and who flee from hard preaching against their sin.
teachings.text:
They inquire of the Lord, but God says He is not to be enquired of by them. Instead, He says to judge them, to hold forth in the word of God against them. To preach hard against their sin.

Many people today claim to "want to know God's will for their lives," and say they are seeking truth, but they flee from hard preaching from the word of God against their sin. Right here we see that God has no interest in being enquired of when your heart isn't right.

God says to cause them to know the abominations of their fathers. We know from Ezekiel 18 that the Lord doesn't hold the sons responsible for the sins of the father, so what is the purpose? As we read we see it is to condemn them for their own.

Much like Jesus rebuking the Jews; **Matthew 23:29-32**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.*

And so, God lays out the dispensations of man; from the day He lifted up his hand, revealing to them in the land of Egypt, to His bringing them forth, to His gift of the promised land, all to proclaim that He would be their God.

And He commanded them to cast away their idols and false gods. The abominations among them, yet they would not.

But He spared them from being wiped out utterly in the midst of Canaan, for His name's sake after Moses appeal to the Lord; **Exodus 32:11-12**
*And Moses besought the Lord his God, and said, Lord, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth? Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people.*

But, God lifted His hand that the parents who sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play, who believed the 10 bad spies and not Caleb and Joshua, that they would not enter into the land.

But, He said to their children *Walk ye not in the statutes of your fathers, neither observe their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols*, to keep His statutes, His judgments; the law. And keep the ordinances and Sabbaths, as a sign that they may know He is the Lord our God.

But they rebelled too. And He did not utterly destroy them, again for His name's sake among the heathen.

And so He scattered them, the northern kingdom, among all the heathen countries, because they consistently went after their fathers' idols and committed their fathers' abominations.

Centuries of rebellion, generation after generation. With God's wrath kindled, but sparing them destruction for His name's sake. Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Persist in supplication
teachings.summary: The 21-day delay matching Daniel's three weeks of prayer teaches us to keep praying when we do not see an immediate answer.
teachings.text:
Either way, the appearance shocks Daniel. The delay the being describes, 21 days, matches the 3 weeks Daniel had been mourning. That his prayer was being answered, but in God's timing is interesting to note. We should not give up in prayer when we aren't seeing them answered immediately. But to be persistent in supplication. This is taught repeatedly in scripture, for example;

**Ephesians 6:18**
*Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints*

Daniel remained at it, and here he was to be given great favor of God, to have revealed unto him the future in what we will see is amazing detail.

Also note that the messenger tells Daniel that what will be revealed is that which is noted in the scripture of truth. The word settled in Heaven. Knowing the end from the beginning.

I believe that when he (He?) says this, and that only Michael, the prince of Israel/Judah, *holdeth with me*, it means the things that would come were made known to the archangel. He drops a bit of prophecy in v20, that once the prince of Persia is dealt with, Greece will follow. As we will see in chapter 11, this is very true, yet in decades to come.

teachings.title: The spirit of Daniel's prayer
teachings.summary: Daniel's humble, contrite prayer seeking mercy for his people should matter more to us than debates over the prophetic timeline.
teachings.text:
The prophecy that came upon Daniel in chapter 9 carries with it multiple applications, both present at his time, in the 1st century with Christ, and in the end times.

Great arguments have been made among Christians and those who profess to be as to the exact meaning of Gabriel's revelation to Daniel.

Was it meaning the destruction of the temple that would be built? Daniel has figured out the 70 years of captivity and desolation of Jerusalem that God foretold Jeremiah was drawing near. And after the captivity, they would return to the city God chose, and build it.

Was it referring to the end times? When the beast tramples Jerusalem underfoot, before the second coming of Christ? All of this?

As I read it, the thing that I focused on wasn't the mystery of these things, and their meaning, but instead the faith of Daniel and his humility before the Lord.

He read the word of God and believing it to be true, began to plea for mercy, with a contrite heart before God.

Daniel reads the curse in the law of Moses, and acknowledges that the Lord has justly judged against Israel and Judah. That their predicament is of their own making. Their own trespass against the Lord. He confesses this sin, and says not of their righteousness, but by His mercy, Lord save us.

Daniel's prayer should be the main focus of this chapter. As Gabriel says, "thou art greatly beloved."

Daniel, we are told repeatedly, had an excellent spirit. He had great faith and humility. He prayed multiple times a day. He sought peace with others. He trusted in the Lord, and served the authority God put in his life with humility, always doing his best.

And here, reading the words of Jeremiah and understanding them in the Spirit and knowing the promises of God given his people, centuries before, he turns to God in supplication and meekness, seeking forgiveness and mercy. Not for himself but for his people.

What a model Daniel is for us. Especially in these last days. The spiritual applications to take from Daniel should exceed whatever timing and charts and arguments over what he was told.

We may have different opinions, may think this applies to the 3.5yrs of tribulation (I do), or whatever pre-trib promises the dispensationalists might take from it.

But if we all held to the spirit of Daniel, and prayed like him and served like him and sought to be pleasing to God, even in a wicked kingdom, even as we are in spiritual Babylon, those things would work themselves out. But we would be pleasing to God.

And our people would be delivered, just as He promises.

teachings.title: Your iniquities have separated you
teachings.summary: Trouble comes not from God's inability to save but because our sins separate us from Him so He will not hear, and Christ our intercessor gives us His armour.
teachings.text:
Fitting chapter, given my previous post.

God telling Judah, and us today, that it isn't any failure or fault if His that we have trouble and tribulation. That He can still save. He can still hear cries for His help.

The fault lies with us, when our iniquity has separated us from our God. When our sins have hidden His face from us. He chooses not to hear.

This applies to our modern times, our nation and others that have fallen away from the truth, while paying lip service to the Lord. Shouting "Christ is King!" and doing little else to get right, to be saved.

Everything that we do when we are separated from God rather than the world, leads to naught. It's as vain as expecting a spider's weaving to become a garment, rather than a snare.

We grope for the wall like we are blind. Light has come into the world, but men preferred darkness because their deeds are wicked.

Read the indictment against us in this chapter again. It is so fitting for modern America.

And the Lord saw some turned from evil and they become prey. The righteous in Him are hated by the world. And so He gave us an intercessor, Jesus, and His salvation and righteousness sustains us.

*For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloak*.

This is the vestments of Jesus, and similarly we who are His are called to put on the armor He has provided us.

**Ephesians 6:11-17**
*Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God*.

But notice vengeance is His clothing, and the promise of His vengeance upon those who love their iniquity more than the truth, will show the oppressors that our Redeemer has come. Amen

teachings.title: Seek the Lord and He gives rest
teachings.summary: God promises to reward those who diligently seek Him and will answer prayers asked according to His will, in His time and as we need, so we simply have to trust Him.
teachings.text:
*Because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side.*

This is a promise of God. Something worthy to place our faith in.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**Matthew 7:7-8**
*Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.*

**1 John 5:14-15**
*And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

It will be in His time. It may not look like what you imagined. It may be what you need not what you want. But He will answer our prayers, and deliver us with His mighty hand from whatever troubles us. We simply have to trust Him. Amen

teachings.title: The prayer of Jabez answered
teachings.summary: Like Jabez, those who abide in Christ and come to God in faith can ask boldly according to His will and be heard.
teachings.text:
The genealogy of the other sons of Judah, unto the days of the kings. The houses of the princes of the land.

With a little more detail, their bounds and habitations. Their crafts. Their victories.

*And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested*

Honorable Jabez was right with God. His prayers answered, and he was not ashamed. Because the Lord delivers.

**1 John 5:14-15**
*And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

As Jesus promised:

**John 15:7**
*If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.*

But we must abide in Him even as His words abide in us, the words of eternal life, the promise of adoption in Christ by faith:

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

So, diligently seek Him. Have faith and the confidence to boldly go before God and ask of Him. It shall be done for you.

**Psalms 55:22**
*Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved*

teachings.title: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief
teachings.summary: We have the Spirit and scripture rather than signs, yet may ask God to increase our faith, and walking in the light and confessing sin gives us confidence that He hears us.
teachings.text:
Hezekiah asked for a sign that the word of God spoken of Isaiah was true. Paul writes in **1 Corinthians 1**:**22-24**;

*For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom: but we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness; but unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.*

In the Old Testament, the Hebrews often asked for a sign, and were given them. Sometimes, God offered a sign that they may know His word was true. But we have the Spirit testifying within us, and the more sure words of prophecy of the Bible.

In our life, when we are praying to God to deliver us from bad things, illness, family members in trouble, whatever, we are reassured by the Spirit confirming the word of God and His promises to us. That according to His will, He is faithful to deliver us. This is sign enough.

But often we need more. As the tearful father said to Jesus, asking Him to bring back his daughter unto him, *Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.* Or as the apostles said to Christ, *Lord, Increase our faith.*

We can ask God for reassurance. We can ask for things we've hoped for, and see the work of the Spirit bringing it about. Increasing our faith. Helping our unbelief. It doesn't mean we doubt our salvation, or that God can't deliver. It just means we are human, and the flesh fears.

This is why it is important to be in good standing with the Father, as Hezekiah was. Able to go before God to ask of Him what we need. By walking 3the Spirit and being right with the things of God, our faith is made stronger, and our trust in him when we are weak will come more naturally.

But when we are in sin, and ashamed, and walk in the flesh, our doubts and fears increase. Our faith that God will save us falters, knowing we don't deserve His mercy.

Thankfully, He is faithful to us, that if we turn to Him, and confess our sins, He will forgive us. **1 John 1:5-9**

*This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

**1 John 5:13-15**
*These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God. And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

So, like Hezekiah, let us walk in the light that we may have confidence in the Lord to deliver us from our troubles.

teachings.title: Our promises and blessings are related
teachings.summary: The two and a half tribes kept their vow and received what they asked, showing God grants obedient children's petitions that agree with His will.
teachings.text:
Here in **Joshua 22**, the first half of the chapter, we find the children of Israel victorious in the promised land, delivered to them by the power of God, who had driven out the kingdoms and left them cities and fields and vineyards, a land flowing with milk and honey.

But not all the tribes of Jacob wished to settle there. Before they'd crossed over into the land west of the Jordan, the tribes of Gad, Ruben and half the tribe of Manasseh had petitioned the Lord through Moses that they may have the land to the east of the river, which was good for cattle, being they had much and were ranchers. Just as Lot saw the plains of Jordan, and saw it was good for herding his flocks, there in the east, and separated himself from Abraham, pitching his tent towards Sodom. This was the same land.

And Moses became indignant at their request, because he felt they were abandoning the brethren to do their own thing, just as the battle was about to be truly met. That it would discourage the remaining Israelites from crossing into the promised land, just as their fathers who spied out the land had 40 years earlier, causing God to curse them to wander in the wilderness.

But, they said not so, while they would build cities for their children and pens for their cattle, the Gadites and Reubenites and half tribe of Manasseh vowed that their men of war would go before the people across the Jordan and fight with them until Canaan was theirs, and they had peace.

So, here in Joshua, having kept their word and fought with their brethren, they are given permission to enter into rest in the lands Moses had given them. And Joshua warns them to follow in the commandments of God and then blesses them further, as they departed;

*Return with much riches unto your tents, and with very much cattle, with silver, and with gold, and with brass, and with iron, and with very much raiment: divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren.*

These men had let their yea mean yea, their promise kept. They believed God and kept His will, but asked in return to have that which they sought on the east of the Jordan, and the Lord gave it to them.

We know the Lord is faithful, and keeps His word. We know the Father answers our prayers and fulfils our needs, and allows us that which is in our hearts as long as it doesn't conflict with His larger plans. If we ask, it shall be given. We may have confidence as believers that if we ask anything according to His will, that our petitions that we desire will be granted. And blessings given for our obedience to His will.

The lesson for believers today is that our promises and blessings are related. Our willingness to do as He commands of us grants us not only reward for our obedience, but He will accommodate that which we seek in this life, so long as it is according to His will. God is flexible, and a good Father;

**Luke 11:11-13**
*If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if he ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent? Or if he shall ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion? If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?*

These men risked their lives for their brothers, they obeyed the will of God. They let their actions speak to their vow, and we're not only given that which they sought for themselves and their families, but were blessed on top of it all for their faith and obedience.

Following this example, being willing and able to do the will of God, as His sons, adopted by our faith in Christ, allows us to enter boldly before the throne, and ask Him and receive.

**Hebrews 4:16**
*Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

teachings.title: Seek first His will: not a prosperity gospel
teachings.summary: From his own life he teaches that seeking God's will first brings spiritual blessings and enough material provision, which is not a prosperity gospel.
teachings.text:
In my own life, I know with certainty that when I first seek the things of God, when I turn to His word, and pray for His will to be done, to be used as He sees fit, that I am blessed beyond measure and the things I seek are given unto me.

This isn't a prosperity gospel. It is the promise of God. Seeking His will first will find you asking for ways to please Him, to be a blessing to others, rather than riches. Asking for patience or understanding and wisdom. Asking to be able to lead others to Christ.

The material blessings will follow, usually just enough to satisfy your needs. Just enough to keep you from trouble, in my case. But the spiritual blessings of helping others to the truth or even just being in the right place at the right time to affect someone positively, they are endless and wonderful. And you receive a good name, as these men did. Amen.

teachings.title: The Lord bless thee and keep thee
teachings.summary: God had the priests put His name on Israel in blessing, and as a priesthood of believers we should remind others that their blessings are from God.
teachings.text:
**Numbers 6**
*22 And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,*

*23 Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying, On this wise ye shall bless the children of Israel, saying unto them,*

*24 The Lord bless thee, and keep thee:*

*25 The Lord make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:*

*26 The Lord lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.*

*27 And they shall put my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them.*

I don't want this law of blessings to be lost in all the vow talk, because it is important.

The Lord instructs the priests to bless the children of Israel in His name, giving various examples. The purpose is to out His name upon them. That they understand where and Who the blessings are from. That it is His name upon them that brings these glad tidings. That they may understand and appreciate Him in their daily lives.

We should do the same, as a priesthood of believers, especially with our family, but everywhere in our lives. People need to be reminded that the blessings that come to them are of God.

teachings.title: Pray directly to the Father: one mediator
teachings.summary: Jesus taught and lived the pattern of prayer: often, privately and earnestly to the Father in His name through the Spirit, with no intermediary like dead saints or a mediatrix.
teachings.text:
Good morning. Pray. Jesus not only taught us the pattern of prayer, the Lord's prayer given to His disciples as a format, a way to approach prayer to God, but He lived a prayerful life, with which we can seek to emulate, showing us the manner of prayer.

Often. Earnestly. Seeking God's will and the acceptance to do it. Alone. Privately. Early in the morning. All night if needed. On your knees. In tears and joy. Praising God in thanksgiving. Seeking forgiveness. Asking for favor, always in His will.

Not publicly and loudly to show how holy you are. When gathered with the assembly, making it short and sweet and to the point. Not in vain repetition as the heathens and pagans who worship at the feet of statues, icons and graven images, but in humble conversation, directly with God our Father. We are His children. We shall want for nothing that is in His will to provide. He knows our needs before we do, and the Holy Spirit aids is in this, our direct contact to God, who dwells within us as saved believers.

**Romans 8:26**
*Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.*

And so we pray to the Father, in the name of the Son, through the power of the Spirit. Boldly going before God in thanks, praise and supplication. Praying directly to God without a need for any other intermediary.

**1 Timothy 2:5**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus*

Not praying to dead spirits, which is divination and necromancy, an abomination to God. Not praying through a "mediatrix;" Jesus didn't say "Our mother..."

We have directly from Christ the form and context, pattern and practice of how we must pray. So, pray.

teachings.title: This kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting
teachings.summary: The disciples failed for unbelief, and Jesus shows that faith to overcome is grown by prayer and fasting, as He Himself did before every undertaking.
teachings.text:
In the retelling of this in **Matthew 17**, the Apostles later ask of Jesus why they failed to cast out that evil spirit.

*And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you. Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.*

We have been talking about the role of fasting and prayer in finding the will of God, understanding it and accepting it. In the end, that's what faith is. Learning, believing and obeying the will of God. Jesus here is telling us that it was a lack of faith, and how to rectify that is by prayer and fasting.

We may encounter things we struggle to overcome. If we had but a tiny bit of faith, this wouldn't be the case. If we seek to, then it is by prayer and fasting that we can grow in faith enough to overcome. Simple as.

Just as Jesus fasted in the desert and prayed without ceasing throughout His ministry, especially when faced with a new undertaking or a difficult task, that's how we are to do it in similar situations. Christianity isn't a gnostic religion of secret revelation. God tells us everything we need to know in order to be successful in our Christian life. To better equip us to do His will. As frustrating as it may be for Him when we don't listen or understand or take it to heart. I thank God for His mercy and patience. If these men tried it, I can't imagine how much more frustrated He gets with me.

teachings.title: Have faith in God and forgive when ye pray
teachings.summary: God promises to answer believing prayer, but we must forgive others as He forgave us, since unforgiveness hinders us and God chastens disobedient sons on earth.
teachings.text:
*Have faith in God.*

*For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith. Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.*

This is not simply an affirmation to put on Instagram. It's not just a "hang in there, God provides" pick me up for a daily inspirational devotion.

It is a promise from God. All He asks is your forgiveness for others as He has forgiven you. To not hold grudges. To let things that aren't important in this life, and keep you from earning the rewards of the next, to let them go.

*When ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses. But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.*

Now, all our sin is forgiven and forgotten in Christ Jesus, at judgment. All believers are in the Book of Life, and so saved.

But on earth, God still punishes the disobedient believers, His chastisement falls on those He loves.

*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

*But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

And we are to confess our sins to God asking for forgiveness;

*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

But how can we humble ourselves to ask for forgiveness for disobeying God when we hold back forgiveness from those who've wronged us? Forgive our trespasses as we forgive others is part of the model for prayer Jesus provides.

Lack of forgiveness is a burden. In the same measure we give mercy and extend grace, the Bible says, is what we receive.

Be mindful of this, and in faith unfeigned, without the burdens of hate and a lack of grace, go boldly before God with your needs. And the Lord God, who cannot lie, promises He will provide.

teachings.title: Ask in prayer, believing, and receive
teachings.summary: From the withered fig tree Jesus taught that whatsoever we ask in prayer believing we shall receive, a literal promise to grow in by faith.
teachings.text:
Matthew continues the narrative the next day, with Jesus returning to the temple, hungry. (A reminder that in all things, Jesus was fully human as well as fully God, and aware of our condition).

Approaching a fig tree, barren of fruit, Jesus says "let no fruit grow on thee, henceforth and forever," and the tree withered on the spot. This is both literal and allegory for the Jews who were to reject Him.

The Apostles seeing this sign, marveled. And Jesus teaches them, had they faith enough they could do this and more. That they could move mountains. That all things asked of in prayer can be delivered unto us, we simply must have faith enough.

*All things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.*

This is a promise from God Himself, in the flesh. Don't treat it lightly or as some kind of daily affirmation, but as literally true. Grow in faith, living faith to faith, building upon it, and witness it in your own life. God is not slack concerning His promises.

teachings.title: Begin with confession: a warning to prayer warriors
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: Effective prayer reminds God of His promises and begins with honest confession, guarding prayer warriors against creeping pride.
teachings.text:
David establishes this truth early in the psalm for a reason, which is made clear as it goes along.

It isn't so much as David brags about his charitable heart to the poor, but in the opening verses, he humbly reminds himself and the Lord he is petitioning of the promises He has made.

Then, the prayer moves to confession. The honest assessment of the heart before a holy, holy, holy God.

This pattern of reminders and confession, before petition, is helpful to keep in mind for our prayer life, if we want it to be successful.

We often hear about "prayer warriors," those who are continuously in prayer, especially for others. Who seek the burdens of others to bring them before the Lord, and it is a wonderful work.

But as we seek to be counted among the elite forces of prayer, we should always keep in mind the humility and confession that makes our prayer life effective.

And so when David writes *be merciful unto me: heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee*, we need to take it to heart in our own approach to the Throne. The man who was the apple of God's eye was honest in his confession. The King of Israel was lowly enough to be convicted as he approached the Throne of Grace.

Watch out for the creeping pride that may come from being recognized as a "prayer warrior," and the audacity that may infect what is a great habit. The loss of the love of others that should drive it, but iniquity creeping in.

Begin with confession. A contrite heart with love unfeigned can move mountains.

teachings.title: Praise, thanksgiving, confession, deliverance
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: We cannot acknowledge salvation without acknowledging the sin we are saved from, and David's psalm models praise, confession, deliverance and judgment in prayer.
teachings.text:
Having acknowledged all He has done for us, and encouraging ourselves and others to turn to Him for salvation through the blessing of the Lord, David's Psalm turns introspective. He confesses the sin that has beset him, and compasses him about with the repercussions of it.

*Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me. For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me.*

We cannot acknowledge salvation without acknowledging what God is saving us from.

Just as David and Paul write of having the law written in their heart, and delighting in His word, they both lament the sinful flesh that requires a Savior.

**Romans 7:24–25**
*O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.*

We ask they the Lord deliver us. That it is His will that be done. That those who are moved to scorn, mocking our trust in the Lord be made ashamed.

That God use us to shame those that wish to do us evil, to His glory.

Praise, thanksgiving, confession, deliverance, and destruction of those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. This is a model of prayer. That His will be done on earth as it is in Heaven.

And in the end, the joy of His salvation overwhelming us with gratitude and praise, that such a holy and Almighty God takes heed of our prayers and notices us. Loving us so much, while we are yet sinners. Thinking of us. Providing for us. Delivering us.

*Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified. But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.* Amen

teachings.title: Sing skilfully with instruments and doctrine
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: Scripture commands singing with instruments in the congregation, songs full of doctrine, avoiding both carnal rock-concert worship and the removal of instruments.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 33** opens with the clearest enforcement of writing, singing and performing songs of praise and worship to Almighty God. On stringed instruments, especially. Performing skillfully and with a loud noise within the congregation, songs with the doctrine of scripture, with the truth of His mighty works being honored.

God's righteousness and judgment, His power and creation, the fear and adoration He commands from those that love the Lord to sing unto Him.

Book of Psalms explicitly names several musical instruments, including the harp, psaltery, timbrel, cymbal, trumpet, cornet, organ, and pipe. These are given instructions by the Psalmist and the music leader, and are used to provide melody and concordance to the congregational singing. An activity that we are encouraged to perform in the New Testament church.

**Colossians 3:16**
*Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.*

Music is a form of learning and worship, as much as prayer, and it is edifying to the soul when focused on this spiritual truth, that it is for His sake that we make melodies.

**Ephesians 5:19**
*Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord*

What it is not, is an excuse to be carnal, to satisfy the flesh with worldly beats and discordant instruments, mimicking a rock concert or depraved discotheque.

Congregational singing stirs the soul, lifting your voice up to the Lord. But many worship services turn into a tantric trance, lifting up hands and swaying, captivated by the music and beats, lasting hours at some churches. With songs that are thinly veiled pop love songs, with little to no doctrine applied.

Other churches take the instruments completely out of the equation, which seems at odds with the details given in the Bible.

There is a middle ground, and a place for various musical accompaniments, while maintaining the orderly and decent service that all things at church should be done in.

teachings.title: Praise, humility, mercy, then judgment
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: Prayer should begin with humbling ourselves and seeking forgiveness rather than complaining, then turn to asking relief and judgment.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 6** continues the prayer and plea theme, with David now up all night with sweat and tears and crying out to the Lord for mercy and for the destruction of his enemies.

Appealing to the mercies of the Lord, to not rebuke us in anger, to not chasten us while He is hot and fiery in His wrath, is wisdom that all Christians should take heed of.

When we sin, when we have been goaded into a reaction by the temptations in our lives, our first instinct should be to ask God to forgive us.

The Devil knows our weaknesses. Our enemies know what buttons to push. How to frustrate us and to get us to react. We are weak. We need God to heal us.

David is crying out that his body and soul are vexed and he is in real pain, and only the Lord can heal him.

Before anything else, the Psalmist has prioritized calling out to God, humbling himself spiritually, physically and mentally, admitting fault and decency on God. This should be our starting position in prayer.

Praise, humility, mercy, then judgment.

Jesus taught us to pray; lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. To bring an end to the tests and trials, and deliver us from the evil set against us.

Many of us may use prayer as a means of complaining, to gripe to God for whatever trouble there is in our life, and to whine about it being unfair that we are suffering at all. I think all Christians can fall into that during our despair. But the problem with this is it lacks the self-reflection and humility, and acknowledgement that we are to blame for many of our own problems. Begging for forgiveness, and forgiving others, recognizing our sin before God, and then asking for relief from His chastening puts the matter right in our heart.

And so, settling this, David transitions to judgment, asking how long will the Lord allow David's enemies to vex him? How long will the trials and temptations continue?

teachings.title: Reminding God of His promises
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: Appealing to God's own promises in prayer shows we know and trust His word, and pleases Him.
teachings.text:
*Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies’ sake. For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?*

Here, David appeals to the promise of God to save us. To remind God of His word shows you actually know it, and trust in it. I think this is pleasing to the Lord.

He means the physical death here, but it has the same application spiritually. How are we to praise Him, if we are dead? How can we show the world His mercies if His promises aren't kept.

I wonder how many appeals to the throne David sat though, that showed him this pattern of petition.

Letting God know how weary it has become, how the vexation has worn you down, is also an effective means of working it through yourself.

David says he is weary with his groaning. He's sick of hearing his own laments. It's all he thinks about, and it is destroying him. The desperate plea to God appeals to His love for us.

He finishes this Psalm as he has others, letting his enemies know his faith in the Lord is unwavering and his confidence in God is strong.

No matter how weary we are, no matter how long we are vexed, no matter how long our temptations, we know we have already overcome in Christ.

The Lord has heard our plea. He promised, and so we know He has. He will receive our prayers. Our enemies will know He is with us, when we keep these models of prayer in mind, and humble ourselves to God's will. He will not make us ashamed.

teachings.title: Unto thee will I pray, morning and night
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: David's morning prayer models calling on God day and night, hallowing His name, asking His will be done and His enemies, the whited sepulchres, brought down.
teachings.text:
The song of **Psalm 5** opens again with prayer, asking the Lord to hear and harken to the singer. David, the psalmist, King of Israel calls out to *his* King and his God.

Many of the Psalms open with this plea, and serve as a model for prayer. "Lord, my God, hear me" is an excellent start any time you go boldly before the Throne. *Unto Thee will I pray.*

And as **Psalm 4** was about praying in the night before sleeping, here in **Psalm 5** it is prayer to start the morning. Day and night, we should be in prayer to our Father. Directing our prayer to Him.

**Matthew 6:9–10**
*After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.*

Hallowed be His name. He is holy, and hates the wicked, the foolish, the workers of iniquity.

We see imprecatory cursing of the liars and the bloody deceitful men, followed by the pledge to submit to God's mercy, and in fear worship Him in His house.

Then, the plea to show us His will, that the Lord's paths be made known to us, by His righteousness and in the face of our enemies seeking to destroy us, asking that God's will be done.

The enemies of God are wicked, and their throat, an open sepulchre, an open grave, giving off the stench of their own corruption.

Jesus uses this term so effectively in **Matthew 23** against the Pharisees.

**Matthew 23:27–28**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness. Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.*

He curses these workers of iniquity, in terms they know from scripture. The death their words bring forth to those that follow them and their lies, Jesus will say to them, begone, *I never knew you.*

The Psalmist asks God to destroy these people that rise against the Lord and against truth. To bring them down by their own wicked plans, to cast them out in their rebellion against God.

But, for those that trust in the Lord, rejoice. Shout for joy! Let those that love His precious name, who love Jesus, forever shout for joy, because the Lord defends us from the wicked. And redeemed us from our sin in His mercy and grace.

*For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield.* Amen.

teachings.title: Praise, gratitude and humility in prayer
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: The Psalms are a foundation for prayer, teaching us to come with praise, gratitude and humility, knowing any righteousness we have is God's.
teachings.text:
Psalms of prayer are the most common. The cries to the Lord to save us from affliction and thanksgiving for having delivered us.

We often don't know how to pray, let alone in the midst of trouble. We often don't take our troubles directly to God. And when we do, we do, are at a loss for what to say.

**Romans 8:26**
*Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered*

But the Psalms are given as a foundation of prayer, to know we have a strong deliverer, a Lord that hears us, Who has given us help in our distress and Who grants mercy to His people.

David calls out to the Lord, *O God of my righteousness,* not telling God of his own righteousness, but the knowledge that whatever righteousness we have, is His.

David acknowledges that the Lord has delivered him in the past, and is asking to be heard to do it again. Praise and gratitude. Humility. These are the foundations of an effective prayer.

Lamenting the ways of those who trouble us, the sons of men who vex the righteous with their filthy conversation. They scoff at the faithful. They love vain things, worldly ideas that profit nothing. They seek after leasing, which means to pursue lies, falsehoods, or deceit. But we are not like they are.

Or at least we shouldn't be.

The Lord has set us apart, His holy people. And He will hear when we reach out to Him.

*Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.*

How often do we lay awake in prayer. Pondering our own sins, and seeking the Lord? How often do we wake in the morning, and praise God for His mercy, asking to be used by Him today?

We have the power given us by Christ, to be sons of God. To boldly go before the throne. Stand in awe, and sin not. Make yourselves a living sacrifice, in all you do. Put your trust in the Lord. Comfort yourself with this relationship with Him, that He has mercifully granted to us.

David writes of the many who have no hope, who don't know the Lord is good to those that love Him. Don't despair as they do. Ask Him for His grace, to shine His light upon us. To look your way. Going to Him in confidence that whatever is His will, it shall be done. Those that trust in the Lord shall not be ashamed.

Let His light fill you, rejoice. We are more blessed than those of the world. More blessed than those in time of bounty. He has made us His children. He has given us eternal life. Rejoice in that. Be still and know He is faithful.

*I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.* Amen!

And in the dark night, when you call out to Him in prayer, know He is with you, even His Spirit that dwells within you.

teachings.title: God's presence came with the praise
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: At the temple's dedication God's glory came when praise was made, not at the sacrifices, so believers who want His presence should keep a song of praise in their hearts.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 69:30-31**
*I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify him with thanksgiving. This also shall please the Lord better than an ox or bullock that hath horns and hoofs.*

Reading **2 Chronicles 5** and the dedication of the Temple as a picture of this salvation process in us isn't perfect, naturally. But a parable is never exact. And all of creation is a parable to the glory of God, in the end, yet nothing compares or approaches the majesty of God.

So, reading the order of things, we see the sacrifices and offerings were not when the cloud of God's Majesty came, (just as He did in the Tabernacle at Moses's dedication in **Exodus 40:34-37**). It was when the praise and worship of the Lord was made.

**Ephesians 5:19-20**
*Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ*

If you want to feel the power of God in your life, if you want to have His presence come upon you, start with this.

The sacrifice was made already. The promise of Christ is God's to fulfill. Now we should praise Him in all things, and we will know we are His by His presence. The Spirit testifying within us that we are children of God.

Even the prayer Jesus teaches us as a model for our prayer life begins by recognizing that our Father is hallowed, holy. Set apart from all others. And that His will is our will, that it be done. The Psalms filled with such praise.

If you wish to have a more fulfilling and productive Christian walk, keep that song in your heart and throughout the day, joyfully praising all things. Giving honor to our holy God.

teachings.title: Singing psalms and hymns continually
teachings.theme: The Psalms as a model of prayer
teachings.summary: David's psalm shows God wants His people to sing songs of praise and thanksgiving continually, in heaven, in the tabernacle and in Christians' hearts today.
teachings.text:
We see the focus of the chapter is the Psalm of thanksgiving David wrote in honor of the ark being returned to the tabernacle, and the sacrifices and offerings restored.

In this psalm, which is also captured in **Psalm 105**, themes of return and deliverance from foreign oppression, which would be inspiring especially to those coming back out of Babylonian captivity. There is also the messianic message of Christ and judgment against the nations.

We can also see a larger purpose to the list of genealogies that opened 1st Chronicles. We have been introduced to many of these names already. And their pedigree is established.

We also see the nature of singing in worship. That God wants us to sing songs of praise and thanksgiving, continuously.

As it is in heaven, as it was in the Tabernacle and the temple. As it is in our hearts today as Christians.

**Ephesians 5:18-20**
*And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit; Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ*

teachings.title: Pray to God against them that persecute us
teachings.summary: Believers may pray as David did for deliverance and against enemies who seek their hurt, asking God to send His angels to defend them, but must pray only to God and never to angels as false teachers lead people to do.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 35** is a model of prayer that carries with it both the plea for deliverance, and imprecatory, or negative prayers against enemies who seek our hurt.

In David's case, we understand that he was falsely accused, had enemies trying to literally kill him and destroy him.

We may not have the threat against our lives, but we can relate.

The Lord is our Judge of judges. We go boldly before the throne of grace, asking anything, that we may plead our cause. Asking God to get involved in our lives, to fight our fights.

We have such an awesome advocate in Christ Jesus and a Father Whose mercy and judgement is righteous and true. It is foolishness not to go before Him in prayer, knowing that He seeks our prosperity. Not the riches and accumulations of things, as the false teachers preach, but our overall benefit and success spiritually, that we may do His will.

So, of course when we have enemies in this life that seek our hurt, it would be natural that we get God involved.

*Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me*. That is to form a flank before us, a hedge of protection, like a wall of men, spear extended. A host to shield us from the advances against us. To show us and comfort us with the truth that He is our salvation.

Let our enemies be confounded and confused. Let them be scattered as the chaff. Let the angel of the Lord be our guardian. His children have guardian angels;

**Hebrews 1:14**
*Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?*

We can call upon Him to give them direction to not only shield us, but it persecute them that seek to do us harm.

But we shouldn't misunderstand that these ministering spirits are ours to control, or to plea to them. Many pray directly to angels, or archangels, which is wicked.

**Revelation 22:8–9**
*And I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things. Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.*

We pray, as David did, to the Living God. He directs His hosts.

The Bible says that false teachers will mislead people into worshiping angels.

**Colossians 2:18**
*Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind*.

Pray directly to God in all things. Pray for Him to dispatch His angels to defend us and attack our enemies, as David demonstrates here.

teachings.title: Love thy enemies, and leave vengeance to the Judge
teachings.summary: We love and pray for enemies in their need, but we need not pray for their success in evil and may ask God to repay those who reward good with evil.
teachings.text:
Like David, our enemies may seek to trap us, secretly. Digging pits for us to fall into, snares to catch us, to spoil us, taking what is ours, even if it is simply our reputation, and in doing so, ruin our testimony to others.

If the seek to ruin us in secret, then let the Lord's destruction come upon them without warning. Let their plans come to nothing and better still, catch them up in their own devices.

*And my soul shall be joyful in the LORD: it shall rejoice in his salvation.*

But, what about *love thy enemies*?

Notice that David is pleading for their destruction, not only for their acts against him, but because of their false witness and betrayal.

They rewarded his good with evil.

When they were sick, he humbled himself in prayer and fasting. He sought intercession for them with the Lord. He shows them love.

This is what we are to do, what Jesus asked of us.

**Matthew 5:44**
*But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you*

This seems contradictory, but it's not. When they are weak, or in need, we are to love them. To pray for their healing and to give to them the charity we wish they'd show us.

We may win them as brothers, or heap hot coals on their heads by our kindness.

But we do not have any obligations to pray they succeed in the evil they do, and while we should not seek vengeance ourselves, we can leave it to the Judge of all to take up our cause and dispatch justice against them.

If we behave as a friend or brother, and mourn with them as their mother, and they still choose to persecute us? That's on them. They can rejoice in our pain, gather together to our hurt, but the Lord will see and repay.

*With hypocritical mockers in feasts, they gnashed upon me with their teeth.*

They may make a feast of our lives, inviting other wicked men to join them, until they seemingly turn the whole world against us, yet we have the Lord.

**Romans 8:31**
*What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?*

teachings.title: Destroy the wicked, spare thine anointed
teachings.summary: Amid constant news of the wicked prospering, we pray for their destruction and our protection from His wrath, with joy instead of fear.
teachings.text:
The Lord is our rock and our salvation. To Him we cry in trouble.

Here in **Psalm 28**, David again shows the importunity of prayer, reminding God of what He means to us, and how His promises to deliver His children, and make us holy, also carry promises of the destruction of the wicked.

Reminding God of our understanding, reinforces the truth in our hearts and provides ready comfort. Because the world is filled with the wicked, and it is easy to become despondent over it.

We are given a constant stream of negativity, of liars and injustice, workers of iniquity, seemingly prospering. Even those that are caught and tried by the system are often given clemency and cover, to continue in their evil deeds.

We ask that God hear our voice, and to respond. To keep us separated from the wrath that is appointed to the workers of iniquity.

Those that speak peace but have mischief in their hearts are all around us. In the news and in our social media feeds. We have a constant black pilling from the world, and can get discouraged.

We also see the world waxing worse and worse, and the repercussions of past sins being visited on our generation, and it can overwhelm some with fear of being caught up in the collapse that is always just around the corner.

But our perspective should be to entreat the Lord with supplication, that as He punishes the wicked, He protects His people. We should want them to receive recompense for their evil deeds, and trust He will protect us from His wrath.

*Because they regard not the works of the LORD, nor the operation of his hands, he shall destroy them, and not build them up.*

The Lord has heard us, and is our strength and shield, the rock of salvation. We should feel joy rather than fear, and praise Him openly for the destruction that comes upon the wicked.

Thy Kingdom come, o Lord. Even so, come quickly. Spare your anointed from your wrath. Save us out of our tribulation. Destroy the wicked.

*Save thy people, and bless thine inheritance: feed them also, and lift them up for ever.* Amen

teachings.title: Praying for judgment with a clean heart
teachings.summary: Imprecatory prayer must include self-examination and willingness to be judged by God's word the same way we ask Him to judge others.
teachings.text:
The psalmist calls for the Lord's judgment, that His sentence be given against the wicked. But it is foolish to cry out for God's perfect justice to be administered, while you yourself are guilty.

It is like a thief going to the police because his partners robbed him of his share of their stolen things. Of a drug dealer complaining about being ripped off in a deal gone wrong.

And so, David wisely shows us the pattern of praying imprecatory prayers includes self-examination and willingness for God to judge him the same way he is judging others.

*Thou hast proved mine heart; thou hast visited me in the night; thou hast tried me, and shalt find nothing; I am purposed that my mouth shall not transgress.*

David credits God's word to keep him from the *paths of the destroyer.* A key doctrine, that it is God's word that we judge ourselves and others by, not our own feelings or desires. We judge righteously when we allow God to tell us good from evil.

David then calls for the Lord to hold up his goings, to keep him on the right path.

So we see that it isn't simply cursing your enemies and expecting God to overlook your sin. But praying for God's judgement, knowing He is just and seeking His confirmation that you are blameless in the matter. Also, praising Him for keeping you from sin in the first place.

All glory goes to God.

Having the faith to be judged fairly by God, knowing that because of God you have walked in His ways, but accepting any fault of your own that He may find...this humility should be at the heart of your prayer life.

teachings.title: Love your enemies, yet pray for God's vengeance
teachings.summary: We love our personal enemies, but may pray imprecatory prayers against the wicked who oppress the righteous, rejoicing that God's wrath will repay.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 9** continues the prayerful praise of the Lord, the call for His righteous judgment, destruction of enemies, rebuke of the heathen, and the eternal salvation to come.

The first of the two great commandments, *Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind*, is reflected in the praise and worship of David's song. Praising God with our whole heart, acknowledging all His wonderful and marvelous works, rejoicing in them.

Note, David is beset by enemies, his cause is right, yet many are against him, he is oppressed, and yet, David begins with praise and rejoicing.

It's been said before, but Jesus does not take away our burdens and cares, He simply makes those burdens light. His yoke is easy. When we are buffeted by the cares and worries of this world, we should stop and praise God for all He has done.

Gratitude and praise should be in the front of our minds and love for Him in our hearts, because in the end, His grace, His saving us is sufficient. We are on the winning side. We have overcome the world in Jesus. So sing praise to His name, *O Thou most High.*

*When mine enemies are turned back*, not if, but when, when they are destroyed by His presence, it is because His enemies are ours.

**Matthew 5:43–44**
*Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you*

We are called to love our personal enemies. David had multiple opportunities to kill Saul, yet he spared him, and appealed to the King in love.

But those that oppress the righteous, and the wicked full of iniquity, God will judge. And we can absolutely pray imprecatory prayers against them, that God will repay. That His vengeance be done, knowing that in the end, there is no escape for the wicked. Their cities will burn, their line will be cut off, there will be no memory of them, and their soul will be in flames of eternal torment.

What little we can do in our wrath? Better to rejoice in the wrath of God, knowing He will handle it.

His throne is established forever in righteousness. He will judge. He will take up the cause of the poor and oppressed. Even in great tribulation, it shall be cut short for the elects' sake.

Because we have placed our trust in His holy name, the Lord Jesus, Who will not forsake those that seek Him. He hears the cry of the humble.

teachings.title: Search me first, then judge the wicked
teachings.summary: In trouble we should ask God to search us and accept our part, then pray for His judgment on the wicked, for God is angry with the wicked every day.
teachings.text:
Again, David writes a playful song of faith in God to deliver him from evil. And again, the pattern of praise, plea, confession, and confidence in the Lord is present.

Because of their nature, the Psalms are dripping with doctrine. Here we see the faith and confidence in God lends itself to appealing to His mercy and holiness. We learn that we should ask Him to search us. To show us what sins we have in our life, that we may be cleansed and pleasing to Him.

David sings out to the Lord to allow the enemies that compass him about to destroy him, if there is anything he had done to deserve this.

When we are being persecuted or falling into diverse temptations, tests and trials, self-examination should be on our mind. Dealing honestly with ourselves and with God, that maybe it is the result of something we have done. Chastening of the Lord for iniquity in our dealings with others. Sins against the Father. Confession is rewarded by God. He loves an honest soul, humbly seeking Him for forgiveness.

So, like David, call out in crisis, but be willing to accept our role in our calamity, and have a clean conscience towards God. Ask Him to judge you according to your integrity and righteousness, that we don't deceive ourselves. That we don't fall into a victim mentality.

Pray for God's judgment, not only upon you, but your enemies. That His will be done on earth, and upon all people, that He will stand up the righteous and lay low the wicked. Knowing that our defense is of God.

*God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day.* This important doctrine is a necessary one, to develop a healthy fear of the Lord, the beginning of wisdom.

The same wisdom here that we find so often in David's son, Solomon and his Proverbs.

That those that deal in iniquity will fall victim to their own mischief. The pits they dig for others to fall in will swallow them up. His violence come back upon his own head.

This expectation of God's judgment is a key portion of our faith. Not only the Lord's mercy upon His children, but His wrath on evil-doers.

God is love. But God is also burning vengeance. His anger is kindled and wrath is stored against the wicked.

**Romans 2:2–6**
*But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things. And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God? Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds*

This truth is as important for understanding God as His love. And is why He deserves our praise as we petition Him for our deliverance.

*I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness: and will sing praise to the name of the LORD most high.* Amen

teachings.title: Jeremiah's imprecatory prayer
teachings.summary: We preach to all, but like Jeremiah we may pray God's wrath on those who utterly reject the truth and seek our lives.
teachings.text:
The Lord tells Jeremiah that if he prophesies to the people and they turn from their wicked ways, He will repent of the evil He planned to do.

Much like God instructed Jonah, and the Gentile nation of Nineveh.

But unlike Nineveh, who received the warning and turned from their wicked ways, God seeing their works and repenting of the evil He would have done to them, the Jews of Jeremiah's time do not. The false prophets and priests preach against Jeremiah and tell the people not to believe his doomsaying.

*Then said they, Come and let us devise devices against Jeremiah; for the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, and let us smite him with the tongue, and let us not give heed to any of his words.*

And Jeremiah prays an imprecatory prayer, asking for God's wrath to come upon them;

*Give heed to me, O Lord, and hearken to the voice of them that contend with me.* *Shall evil be recompensed for good? for they have digged a pit for my soul. Remember that I stood before thee to speak good for them, and to turn away thy wrath from them.*
