*Therefore deliver up their children to the famine, and pour out their blood by the force of the sword; and let their wives be bereaved of their children, and be widows; and let their men be put to death; let their young men be slain by the sword in battle. Let a cry be heard from their houses, when thou shalt bring a troop suddenly upon them: for they have digged a pit to take me, and hid snares for my feet. Yet, Lord, thou knowest all their counsel against me to slay me: forgive not their iniquity, neither blot out their sin from thy sight, but let them be overthrown before thee; deal thus with them in the time of thine anger.*

We should preach the Gospel to every creature, even if they on the surface appear hopelessly wicked, but we shouldn't hold out hope for those who reject the truth utterly, and seek our destruction for giving it. These sons of Belial are twice-dead. May God destroy those who seek our lives for His holy name's sake. Amen.

teachings.title: Shall not God avenge His own elect
teachings.summary: The parable of the unjust judge teaches us to pray always for the kingdom to come and for God's swift vengeance and wrath on the wicked.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 6:10**
*And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?*

**Luke 18** opens continuing the teaching to Jesus' disciples on the coming of the day of the Lord, and He offers a parable that they understand to pray always for the kingdom to come, and not faint, not be worried or impatient. He gives an example of a man who is a judge, not God-fearing, not a respecter of persons, who when bothered repeatedly by a woman seeking him to avenge her against her adversary, decides to do it to avoid her constant bothering.

Jesus says if this unjust judge will do the right thing to avoid the widow's incessant pleading, how much more will God the Father avenge His elect in answer to their prayers?

When Jesus teaches us to pray, He says "Thy kingdom come" should be a part of it. We are told to pray for God's swift judgment, the day of the Lord, our salvation and redemption by the resurrection, and His glorious and righteous wrath being poured out on the earth and the wicked that remain.

Jesus assured us, He will come speedily. God, to Whom a thousand years is like a day to man, will not tarry. He will repay. Vengeance is His.

But, Jesus asks, *Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?*

teachings.title: Avoid bargaining with God, give Him the glory
teachings.summary: We may persistently ask God's help and promise praise, but bargaining with our works gives us room to boast and shares the glory that is His alone.
teachings.text:
Pleading with the Lord to not tarry, to come quickly to our aid, with the knowledge that we will sing His praises for His salvation, is a key piece of prayer.

We have discussed importunity in prayer, asking God again and again to please help us in our time of need. When we are past the point of what we think we can stand, to give us relief.

We have nothing to give but our love and praise in exchange.

Some try to bargain with God, usually when we pray amiss, seeking our will rather than His. "I'll go to church more, I will read my Bible more." I will stop this sin or that. We offer sacrifices of our own time or effort or even money.

But that's not what God seeks. Those are things that are the least we could do, even as unprofitable servants.

What we do have is praise for His power and His strength. And He is due all the glory.

*I will give thee thanks in the great congregation: I will praise thee among much people.*

When we bargain with God for what we want, when we add our efforts and barter for His, we give ourselves a means to boast. We can fool ourselves into thinking our works played a part in the outcome. We begin to forget how helpless we were, and how God deserves all the glory. We begin to see our efforts as the reason God "owed it to me" rather than His love and righteousness.

And so, we may keep asking God for His intervention, and we may remind Him that our gratitude will be expressed to His worship and to show others His strength and power.

But avoid bargaining or anything that shares the glory with Almighty God. Trust that He loves you and will, in His due time, make whatever it is you are going through to be handled to our good and His will.

**Romans 8:28**
*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

teachings.title: Better not to vow than not to pay
teachings.summary: God takes vows seriously and wants sincere prayer and humble service, not rash vows, long showy prayers or boasting of works to be seen of men.
teachings.text:
**Ecclesiastes 5** sees a brief detour in the sermon, a rabbit trail of wisdom stemming from Solomon's preaching.

Verse 1 is an oft-quoted favorite of pastors; a reminder to take church seriously, to come to hear and learn in the house of God, which Paul tells Timothy in **1 Timothy 3:15,** is *the pillar and ground of the truth.*

He warns against the fool's sacrifices, his offerings and his words, not considering God's holiness and His word, uttering long prayers and excuses, a multitude of words, to make up for the lack of sincerity and humility.

Solomon compares the restless dream-filled sleep of those stressed out by their busy lives to the fool's prattling speech. Just as dreams are nonsense, so too are the fools vows;

*For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.*

And so, we are given another proverb against vowing vows to God that you don't mean, or are beyond your ability to keep. Fools do this, promising God a multitude of promises; turning from this sin or that, promises that for God's favor the fool will do something or give an offering for it, that is never paid.

*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.*

Jesus teaches this.

**Matthew 5:34-37**
*But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.*

James repeats the doctrine.

**James 5:12**
*But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.*

God takes vows seriously. He doesn't care for excuses, long public prayers, vain repetitive prayers. He wants sincere prayers and humble servants.

Better to say nothing than to be a fools.

**Proverbs 10:19**
*In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise*

Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps his mouth shut.

**Proverbs 17:28**
*Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding*

There are blowhards in every church in the world. Professing Christians who cannot help but make themselves known, and promote the things they do. Who make grand promises to help the church, or make this offering or that, to do works for the Lord, all to be seen by men.

It's foolishness. And vanity.

Verse 6 warns against the foolishness of talking yourself into sin, or excusing your sin as being done ignorantly. God hates this. The angel here, I believe, is the human messenger, the Levitical priest where the sacrifice is being made. But the principle remains, even now before God and His judgements.

A humble and contrite heart, this pleases God.

teachings.title: Jephthah's needless vow
teachings.summary: God does not need our vows to deliver us, so we should not bargain with Him by vowing, but if we vow we must pay it.
teachings.text:
As Jesus says, *Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.*

God does not need our vows, our promises to do good or to perform works in order to deliver us. He simply asks we trust in Him and let our *yea mean yea.*

Jephthah would have won victory over the children of Ammon by the power of the Lord. He did not need to add his own works as part of God's plan. But God holds us to vows;

**Ecclesiastes 5:4**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.*

So it should not be done in an idle fashion. But if possible, a vow to God in exchange for His favor should not be done at all. Godly living and honest character do not require such a thing. It is by God mighty hand that we are delivered. Not of works of ourselves.

Jephthah paid a price he needn't have, because he placed a portion of his faith in his own hands.

teachings.title: Vows to God are grave
teachings.summary: Vows to God must be taken seriously and paid, as Ecclesiastes, Numbers and the death of Ananias and Sapphira show.
teachings.text:
Vows were made for various purposes and reasons, just as the Nazarites. People vowed special offerings, gifts to the priests of money and items, fasting was often accomplished by vow. And vows to God should always be taken seriously and not haphazardly.

**Ecclesiastes 5:4-6**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.*

**Numbers 30:2**
*If a man vow a vow unto the LORD, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.*

Even in the New Testament, there were some who swore vows, and the expectations of the grave nature of it was the same.

We see in **Acts 5** the vow made by Ananias and his wife to offer the price of a sold property to the church at Jerusalem, only to withhold a portion for themselves.

*But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land? Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God. And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things. And the young men arose, wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him.*

The Bible says 3 hours later, Sapphira was confronted with the same dereliction of their vow, and suffered the same fate as her husband.

The Bible shows Paul taking various vows, as in **Acts 18:18** which appears to be Nazarite;
 
*And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.*

And Paul takes a vow in **Acts 21** at the behest of James, the brother of Jesus, that results in his arrest at Jerusalem.

As we see throughout Acts and the early epistles, Paul sought to bridge the gap between the believing Jews and Gentiles, with the Gospel of grace, because of his love for his brothers after the flesh, and his disentanglement from the practices of the Jews came over time, mainly through his opposition to Judaizers.

teachings.title: Pay thy vows and plead His promises
teachings.summary: God holds us to the vows we make in His name, yet He delights when we remind Him of His promises in prayer, and in Christ we have boldness and access to ask of the Father.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 28**
*And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God:*
*And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.*

The moment of truth. Will God deliver or will Jacob be killed? And if he puts his full trust in God, recognizing His power, having faith he will be delivered safely to his father's house in peace, he will have to honor his vows.

Sometimes we as Christians, especially when we haven't been walking with Christ, maybe backslidden or just stubbornly trying to fix and control things in our lives, we will make vows to God if He would provide. God holds us to the vows we make in His name.

**Numbers 30:2**
*If a man vow a vow unto the LORD, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth*

**Ecclesiastes 5:4**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed*.

**Psalms 76:11**
*Vow, and pay unto the LORD your God: let all that be round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.*

At the same time, God delights in our reminding Him of His promises, in prayer and supplication. Because God is not slack concerning His promises. He keeps His side of every covenant. And our acknowledging of this and trusting Him to do so brings Him joy and glory. It is not tempting God to remind Him, by our recognition, realizing all He does is in grace and mercy to us, as sinners, that He is true to His word and won't let us down.

And in Christ we have the authority to boldly go before the Father, and all we ask shall be delivered.

**Ephesians 3**

*8 Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;*

*9 And to make all men see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ:*

*10 To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,*

*11 According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord:*

*12 In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.*

*13 Wherefore I desire that ye faint not at my tribulations for you, which is your glory.*

*14 For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,*

*15 Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named,*

*16 That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;*

*17 That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,*

*18 May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;*

*19 And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.*

*20 Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,*

*21 Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.*

teachings.title: One mediator and boldness before the Father
teachings.summary: Contrasts the believer's access to the Father through the one mediator Christ Jesus with Catholic reliance on Mary, saints and priests.
teachings.text:
God tells us, who are saved, who have the Spirit of adoption, that we have one mediator with the Father, Christ Jesus, and one intercessor for prayer, the holy Spirit. We go boldly before the Father with confidence as sons.

But Catholics don't. They use idols and "Mary," and "saints" and priests as intermediaries. Because they know in their hearts they cannot go to the Father as sons.

Most Catholics are just misled. Not full blown apostate reprobates. And they know in their hearts they cannot enter boldly before the throne.

So the Catholic church tells them to go through stone and wood and to human intercessors, for their conscience's sake. Very sad.

teachings.title: Praying to be used of God
teachings.summary: Reads Romans 8 and 1 Samuel 12 and shares that walking in the Spirit shifts prayer from fears and needs to asking God to use us to bless others.
teachings.text:
**Romans 8:18-28**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope, Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it. Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God. **And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.***

**Psalms 56:11**
*In God have I put my trust: I will not be afraid what man can do unto me.*

**1 Peter 3:15-16**
*but sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

**1 Samuel 12:24**
*Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.*

I think the most surprising thing you find when you walk in the spirit and God is blessing you, the thing that you start to actually pray for, instead of your fears and needs, is that He use you. Praying that you can be the means of blessing someone else. That God use you to benefit someone else, because you know He's already got you.

Have that faith.

teachings.title: Thanksgiving in prayer
teachings.summary: Wishes more of church prayer time were thanksgiving for blessings, and gives reasons believers hold back public thanks.
teachings.text:
I wish more of the prayer time in a service were of thanksgiving than for asking. It's nice to have people pray for you and your needs, but God already knows our needs. Even if we don't. And He grants us petitions for sure. But the blessings out of the blue, little things even, all add up.

I think sometimes Christians don't give public thanks for blessings in their lives for a few reasons. One, much of the time it is personal. It's something between you and the Father and He blessed you. Maybe even embarrassing, dealing with a sin or whatever. But other times I think people hold off because they don't want to be seen as bragging, or boasting against those who maybe aren't as blessed.

What if I told you that the people you think aren't as blessed as you need to know they can be.

Using discernment, tact and grace, with all sincere humility, glory God for all that goes right in your life, especially answered prayers made just in daily communication with Him.

That morning prayer and Bible reading gives you confidence to ask of God, and He rewards in abundance. In ways big and small.

People need to hear that. It gives hope to the hopeless. It draws people to Christ. Because you walk in the Spirit and do what you can to not be spotted from the flesh.

It is edifying to people who may be in a bind to know that faith does favor with our Lord, Who loves us. You read His word and learn it and understand where He's coming from. What He asks. His yoke is light.

And the gratitude given in thanksgiving from us to God is a light to those in the dark.

teachings.title: Talking with God as Father and friend
teachings.summary: Shares how he talks with God the Father and with Jesus all day, and that the fear of the Lord is reverent respect for His authority alongside closeness as a dear friend.
teachings.text:
DB VM starts with a very good point about how our relationship with God the Father should be. I have conversations with God all day, everyday. He and I joke, He points out things and I come to him with my problems, talk about the nature of things and His creation and what things must be like from His point of view, given the examples and parables He sprinkles throughout my day. And talking with Jesus, who's my brother and my Lord, who the Bible says is not ashamed to call me brother, because of the love He showed me, and the grace of God.

Fear of the Lord is respect for his judgments and His position and authority over creation, and we should be reverent and respectful but He's also our closest and dearest friend. I love God more than my wife, my children, definitely myself and you should too because He loves you that much.

Anyway I thought it was a really good point, so listen to my friends voice message

teachings.title: God sees when we go quiet
teachings.summary: Compares a child who goes silent when up to something to a believer who stops praying. Encourages talking to God about sin and bad decisions, with an apology, because he still loves us as a parent loves a child.
teachings.text:
Having adult children, it gives you some perspective on how God feels, sometimes.

You notice that when your kids are up to something they know you wouldn't approve of, they go silent suddenly. The everyday or every other day conversations dry up for a few days.

That's how God sees it when we're not praying to him everyday. He sees right through it

Don't let sin in your life stop you from talking to God about it. Don't let bad decisions you've made go without at least an apology. He still loves you, just as a parent still loves their child. Don't let embarrassment keep you from Him

How many times have you ghosted your own parents who you love, ghosted them for a few days cuz you just don't want to hear it.

Everybody raise their hand

teachings.title: David's cry of contrition
teachings.summary: Psalm 51 shows how a believer under God's judgment should come in humble worship and confession, trusting that God is faithful to forgive and cleanse even sins like David's.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 51** is the clearest and most sober cry of contrition and supplication for forgiveness by a believer, in the face of a judgment by the Almighty God, that we have in Scripture.

It is David at his lowest. "A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba."

We know the story. David doesn't go off to war as kings were expected to. He stays at his place and sees Bathsheba, the wife of his soldier, Uriah the Hittite, bathing on her nearby roof. Filled with lust, he has her. And as a consequence of that adultery, David conspired to have Uriah killed in battle, and wed his pregnant widow.

Nathan confronts the King, and the Lord curses David for his sin;

**2 Samuel 12:7–10**
*And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul; And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon. Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.*

The judgment of God was given, the child should die.

**2 Samuel 12:14–15**
*Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die. And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.*

David fasts and prays and stays by the child's side, but in the end the illness takes the boy.

**2 Samuel 12:18–19**
*And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead? But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.*

David, devastated, cleans himself and goes into the house of the Lord to worship. It is in this context that this Psalm was written.

Rather than a root of bitterness against the judgement of God, as many are tempted to take on in the face of such fierce judgement, David concedes and comes to the Lord, asking for mercy. As he has so often in **Psalms**, he begins in worship, praising God for His lovingkindness and mercy. Reminding himself, and the Lord of His great qualities, and appeals to the ultimate judge to blot out his transgressions.

This is a formula of prayer that we should commit to our prayer life. Under better circumstances and joyous events, or in grave repentance and regret for whatever sins we have committed, the Lord should be approached in humility and meekness of spirit. Hallowing His holy name.

The request is to forgive the confessed transgressions, knowing He is merciful and faithful to forgive His children.

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

This same promise applies to believers, today. The sure knowledge that our heavenly Father is faithful to forgive us, even the sins of the level of David. To wash us throughly, to cleanse us. To blot the iniquity from our record, and heal us, and our relationship with God.

But note, it is if we confess our sins. David acknowledged his transgressions. We cannot lie to God and we should not lie to ourselves. We cannot hide from our sin when we've faced judgment, and our conscience keeps the sin ever before us in guilt.

teachings.title: The peace of God keeps the heart
teachings.summary: Gathers Colossians 3:15-17, Philippians 4:6-7 and Isaiah 26:2-3 on the peace of God as a promise to those who trust Him.
teachings.text:
**Colossians 3:15–17**
*And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.*

**Philippians 4:6–7**
*Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. **And the peace of God,** which passeth all understanding **shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.***

**Isaiah 26:2–3**
*Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in. **Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.***

The Lord keeps those whose mind stays on Him, Whom they have trusted. God keeps your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

No matter what you call this, it is a promise of God. Let God be true and every man a liar!

teachings.title: A new song of His great salvation
teachings.summary: Psalm 40 rejoices in God's deliverance from the miry pit of sin onto the rock Christ, showing that God never required sacrifices to save but only faith in His promises, which comes by hearing His word and calling on His name.
teachings.text:
After the somber and broken-hearted appeal of **Psalm 39**, **Psalm 40** gives us the rejoicing of those that trust in the Lord, and declares His power to all.

How wonderful is our patient waiting on the Lord, having called out His name for deliverance, to be rewarded by seeing Him turn towards us to save us in love!

He frees us from the miry pit of sin, He delivers us out of tribulation and temptations. He brings us from the shifting sands of doubt and fear, and sets us upon a rock. Our rock, Christ Jesus. The solid ground where He establishes our goings, and directs our paths. Praise Jesus for His great salvation!

We who are saved have a new song in our heart, the gospel which we preach, the good news of eternal life and forgiveness in Christ, *even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD*.

*Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.*

Is there any better news than this? Repenting from lies to trust in the Lord, and the blessings that we are given by His grace in exchange. Eternal life, His perfect word, His judgments. The Spirit of truth. The rejection of the proud. The deliverance from the evil of others. Made sons of God and joint-heirs with Jesus. Many are the wonderful works that our Lord God has done!

The tone of worship and blessings towards God in this prayer song of gratitude is as infectious as it is doctrinally rich.

The thoughts of the Lord towards us, that He even considered a wretch like me, the wonderful things He has for us cannot be numbered. There's not enough time or words in this life for us to declare all He has done for us.

All we can do is cry out, "Thank you!" And share this good news with others.

*Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.*

The blood of bulls and goats never took away sin. It may have cleansed the flesh to be in the presence of God in the temple made with hands, but to enter into His presence forever, in the Temple of Heaven, all He has ever required was faith in His promises.

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God*.

Have they not heard? The word of God has gone out to the world and not returned void. But those that harden their hearts, and stiffen their necks and refuse to obey the gospel of God.

As Jesus and the prophets taught:

**Matthew 13:13–16**
*Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.*

God has blessed us with the conviction of the Spirit, that even in the miry pit, we heard Him, and see with our eyes the mighty God, being converted and healed. Calling upon the name of the Lord.

**Romans 10:13**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

teachings.title: Loving the truth and hating every false way
teachings.summary: David's psalms of trust are models of prayer that Christ Himself quoted, and loving God's truth, a gift of the Spirit, means hating false prophets who teach damnable heresy while loving those they mislead enough to tell them the truth.
teachings.text:
**Luke 23:46**
*And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.*

David's Psalms of trust in the Lord God, to be delivered and never ashamed, redeemed in His righteousness, are models of prayer, and Jesus upon the cross quotes them (or rather, they quote Him). How much more should we?

The cries to listen to our prayers and save us out of trouble, acknowledging that He is our rock and our fortress, our Savior, our ready help in time of tribulation, they echo through time and are as relevant to Christians today as they were to the King of Israel, and the congregation that sang them 3,000 years ago.

*Into thine hand I commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O LORD God of truth.*

Trusting the God of truth to keep His word, having faith in His promises, is the foundation for our Christian life. Relying on His word to feed us with truth. Knowing the truth that sets us free.

And loving the truth puts us in a position where we hate those that lie about the Lord.

**Psalm 119:104**
*Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.*

This love of the truth and understanding of His word is a gift of the Spirit of God.

**1 John 4:6**
*We are of God: he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us. Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.*

All things are made known to us by the Spirit, through Christ who is the way, the truth, the light.

And so we should be vexed by false prophets who teach damnable heresy.

**1 Timothy 4:1–2**
*Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron*

These false prophets are reprobates concerning the faith. Their lies make their followers twofold more the child of Hell than themselves. They are enemies of God, and we should hate them with a perfect hatred, while loving those misled by them enough to proclaim the truth.

teachings.title: Prayer for the lost and going soul winning
teachings.summary: Says a prayer for the lost is also a call for the believer to go and show them the gospel, and urges members to support the church's children's services and soul winning.
teachings.text:
Everyone wants children's services, no one wants to work them.

If you want more out of your church than you're willing to put in and then backbite and complain, instead of supporting your pastor and helping out (and taking care of your unruly children is bare minimum BTW), you have a bad spirit and aren't right with God.

You can be 3-to-thrive, and still not be right with Jesus, if the spirit you have is wrong.

If you aren't volunteering to help and your kids are a nightmare, you need to be rebuked and convicted. Not coddled and catered to.

This goes doubly for soul-winning.

There are people who ask that their family and friends be added to the prayers for the lost that folks at Wednesday night prayer service gladly pray for, when the people asking never darken the door of the church outside of Sunday morning, and never show up for door knocking.

There are Christians in the lives of those strangers we minister the gospel to, praying that their loved ones get saved, too.

If you want soulwinners to bring the truth of Christ to your loved ones, but can't be bothered to go out and warn who you can, don't be surprised when your prayers go unanswered in that regard.

**Romans 10:13–17**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. **How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!** But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report? So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

Every prayer for the lost is a prayer that the Spirit not only softens the heart of the unsaved, but that He also brings soulwinners into their lives to show them the gospel from scripture.

The Spirit not only is convicting the lost loved one, but should be convicting you as a saved believer to go out into the highways and hedges, bringing that gospel of peace to whoever you can. To be an ambassador for Christ in the ministry of reconciliation.

**2 Corinthians 5:17–20**
*Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation; To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation. Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.*

teachings.title: They that wait on thee shall not be ashamed
teachings.summary: Psalm 25 models trusting prayer: lifting our souls to God, confessing sin that may bring chastening, and waiting on Him, never ashamed.
teachings.text:
The powerful prayer of **Psalm 25** is a model for all that trust in the Lord, and a doctrinally-rich reminder of why we should. That we who wait on the Lord will not be ashamed.

Verse after verse, the psalmist has us call upon the name of the Lord, as we read or sing through the Psalm. And verse after verse we are reminded of His mercy and faithfulness.

We lift up our souls, every fiber of our being, unto the Lord, and He delivers us from our enemies. Those that trust in Him are never ashamed, but those that reject His truth are.

We are shown His ways, taught His statutes, walk His paths, and we are preserved in this life, and established in the next.

The meek and his seed shall inherit the earth, and in meekness we humbly admit our sins and ask for God's mercy, to forget them. His lovingkindness is established from old, and the God of our salvation keeps us by His power, unto redemption. What an amazing God we have. How can we not serve Him in truth. Truth of Who He is, who we are, and the reconciliation we have with and in Him, despite our sins.

The Lord teaches sinners like us in His way, and the meek share this truth with the world.

His secret, His covenant, is shown to us. And that good news is spread abroad by those that fear Him, that others may know the mystery of the gospel, and be saved.

*Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.*

**Proverbs 3:6**
*In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.*

**Galatians 5:16**
*This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh*.

Looking to Jesus the author and finisher of our salvation, we are lifted from the nets, the snares of sin set for us by the wicked. Walking in the Spirit. Acknowledging the ways of the Lord.

With importunity and persistent prayer, we remind Him of the goodness He has shown us, and ourselves of the grace we have found in Him. Our troubles become lighter, as His yoke is easy. He brings us out of our distress.

The pain we feel, He understands. The affliction that besets us is often due to sin. Seeking forgiveness, because our troubles may be chastening by a loving Father. Getting right so we may be lifted up by Him. Delivered, because we put our trust in Him. Never ashamed, because His word is true. Waiting on the day of the Lord, and the redemption of all Israel. All His people who trusted in the Lord. Amen

teachings.title: What worship means in scripture
teachings.summary: Shows from the Hebrew shachah, translated worship, bow and obeisance, that Catholics change the meaning of worship to excuse idolatry.
teachings.text:
When a Catholic tells you you don't understand what "worship means" they are actually changing the meaning of the word to obfuscate their idolatry.

The Hebrew term (שָׁחָה / shachah) is used 172 times in the Old Testament - translated as “worship” 99 times, “bow” 31, “bow down” 18, “obeisance” 9, “reverence” 5, “fall down” 3.

Defined as to depress/prostrate oneself (especially in homage to a superior, royalty, or God) i.e., to bow, kneel, or fall down in respect and deference.

The primary Greek term (proskuneō) accounts for the great majority of NT occurrences of “worship” (60 times) and is defined as "to fall upon the knees, touch the ground with the forehead/kneel or prostrate oneself" in homage or obeisance (whether to express respect or make supplication).

**Exodus 20:4–5**
*Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me*

The term is explicitly rendered as "bow" in the 2nd Commandment, and carries with it no qualifiers or anything indicating that the "level of honor" given when bowing and making supplication to an image or idol has any bearing when considering the commandment.

There is no question that bowing before an image or idol, regardless of what it is meant to represent, is strictly forbidden.

**Deuteronomy 5:7–10**
*Thou shalt have none other gods before me. Thou shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the waters beneath the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.*

There is no mention of special religious worship for images of God, versus images of men, where it is allowed.

Jeroboam created a new religion for Israel, with images of golden calves that were meant to represent the Lord God of Israel, and God destroyed them for it:

**1 Kings 12:28–32**
*Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And he set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan. And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Bethel, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.*

And because of this false religion of idolatry, God judged Israel

**1 Kings 15:30**
*Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger.*

It is no wonder that every nation that becomes majority Catholic is judged by God, and is either wiped out with famine, war, disease or invasion and ethnic replacement.

teachings.title: Make haste, my beloved: praying for His return
teachings.summary: The Song ends in prayer for the beloved to come quickly, the believer's prayer of Maranatha for the day of the Lord, the gathering of His people and His wrath on the ungodly.
teachings.text:
The Song of Solomon ends with prayer. She calls upon the Lord, acknowledging that the companions of God hear His voice. His sheep. She asks, humbly, to hear His voice as He calls.

We should always listen for that still, small voice. We should pray that God gives us ears to hear His will.

Her final prayer is that her love come quickly. To make haste in His return, to come down upon the mountains, as a roe or young hart, gazelle among the spices.

The prayer for *Thy Kingdom, come.* Or *Even so, come, Lord Jesus,* is found throughout scripture. *Maranatha,* come quickly.

**2 Peter 3:12**
*Looking for and hastening unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?*

This is our hope, for the day of the Lord. His gathering of His people, the resurrection of the saints into glory. His terrible and fearful wrath on the ungodly.

As mature Christians, we should be as the woman, gladly giving ourselves to the Lord, and praying to hear His voice, praying for His return. She has come to understand love, through Him. And has gladly given herself to Him.

teachings.title: Forgiving and praying for others' sins
teachings.summary: Teaches from 1 John 5:16-17 and John 20:23 that believers should forgive others and ask God to forgive them.
teachings.text:
The New Testament explicitly teaches that we who are saved should forgive the trespasses of others against us. That we should pray to God to forgive them.

**1 John 5:16-17**
*If any man see his brother sin a sin which is not unto death, he shall ask, and he shall give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it. All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death.*

**John 20:23**
*Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained"*

This is a duty of all believers. To say "forgive them Father, for they know not what they do."

teachings.title: Give me neither poverty nor riches
teachings.summary: Agur's prayer for neither poverty nor riches shows we should be content with what God gives, since riches make men forget God and want makes them steal, as Paul learned contentment.
teachings.text:
Continuing **Proverbs 30** and the sayings attributed to Agur the son of Jakeh.

Vs 7-9 is a form of prayer to the Lord to grant Agur favor in this lifetime; That God removes from him vanity and lies and to give neither poverty or riches, yet have sufficient food to eat.

*Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.*

This should be the attitude we strive for. To take away the worthless and useless things in our life that take us away from fully serving God. That we deal honestly, not only with others but ourselves and therefore with God. Hiding nothing. Rationalizing or excusing nothing. Not heeding delusion that covers sin.

Being satisfied with what God has blessed you with. Being content to have sufficient food to eat. Living simply unto the Lord. As many Proverbs before this have shown, the rich place their trust in their possessions. Themselves. They deny God and say "Who is the Lord?"

Make no mistake, that even the temporary and sudden wealth an average or lower middle-class person may receive, a windfall or an unexpected inheritance or bonus, is often sufficient to knock them off the pathway of God. To make them forget the blessings and the Blesser. How much worse to have the wealth always about you, where you want for nothing and grow complacent towards God?

And be thankful that you're not poor, and left to steal to eat. To curse God for your station and take His name in vain.

Sometimes, in our Christian walk, we are tempted. Covetousness turns to greed. How often do we pray, not with thanksgiving for what we have, but desiring "just a little more, God, please?" That He would increase our wealth so we can afford some luxury or extravagance that we've convinced ourselves that we deserve. "Everyone else has one!" Coveting. "If we only had a little more!" Greed.

**Philippians 4:12**
*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.*

Paul writes the end goal that Agur sought. To know how to be both rich and poor, everywhere in all things, to know *whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.*

Why? *I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.*

The vanity of riches and the lies that rationalize sin away, are traps we should call upon the Lord to save us from. Contentment and gratitude go a long way to remove these things far from us.

teachings.title: Jehoshaphat's assembly of prayer and praise
teachings.summary: Because Judah had been brought back to God by revival, they could fast, pray and sing in tribulation and see God deliver them, as a believer walking in the Spirit can boldly ask God for deliverance.
teachings.text:
The final entry in the Chronicles of Jehosaphat's reign. We see here that the godly king's faith, and his efforts in leading revival among the people brings them to be able to call upon the Lord in adversity, and know He would not forsake them, but deliver them as He has promised.

While not perfect in all his ways, Jehosaphat consistently sought the Lord. Even when he yoked with Ahab in their failed battle with Syria, he insisted the wicked king inquire of the prophet Micaiah.

And so, when the armies of Ammon and Moab and Mt Seir assemble against Jerusalem and her king, Jehosaphat calls the people together. A called out assembly in fast, and prayer, and singing songs in praise of God. Calling on Him to remember His promise, showing they have faith in His word.

Because of all the legwork, soul-winning, hard preaching, keeping the word of the Lord, Judah is right with God and able to do this in good conscience.

They weren't perfect. There were high places still in the land. Not all their hearts were continuously with the Lord.

But, generally the people were faithful and believed. And so in time of tribulation, with the armies gathered as the sand of the sea, the Lord confounded them, turning them on one another until they were all dead.

Just as He will defeat the armies of Satan after the millennium. While we stand firm and sing praises to His name.

A Christian who walks in the Spirit, who first seeks the things of God, praying and reading the Bible, going to church. Putting the profit of others above their own, can boldly go before God to ask for deliverance, knowing He is faithful and true.

teachings.title: Praying to saints is superstition
teachings.summary: Says Catholic prayers to saints treat them as house gods or demigods and amount to a spell no less superstitious than pagan practice.
teachings.text:
Catholics will say they don't pray for the power of the saints to be given to them. But they always vacillate between "intercession" and actually having the spirit they claim to be praying to, to work a miracle themselves. They treat these idols and spirits as house gods or demigods. It is wicked as Hell

Note the casual blasphemy that a man was as perfect, complete in righteousness, as Christ, and that God gave this demigod a magic ability to find lost items, through an incantation. A spell basically, that invokes this magic power for the caster.

It is no less superstitious and profane than common pagans, witches and sorcery.

teachings.title: Giving thanks: any day honored to God is acceptable
teachings.summary: Answers a claim that Thanksgiving is pagan by pointing to Romans 14 and the verses that call believers to give thanks in everything.
teachings.text:
JK don't listen to Judaizing vipers who say things like this. They are fools.

**Any day** you esteem in glory to God and thanksgiving for the blessings He has provided, honoring Jesus, or celebrating His perfect work that is our salvation, is acceptable to the Lord.

**1 Thessalonians 5:18**
*In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.*

**Philippians 4:6 **
*Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God*.

**Psalms 107:1**
*O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever*.

Happy Thanksgiving to all my brothers and sisters in Christ. God is great, Amen.

teachings.title: Christ our surety, the Spirit our earnest
teachings.summary: The law of vows and surety pictures salvation, where Jesus is the surety of a better testament and the Spirit the earnest until the day of redemption.
teachings.text:
The last chapter of Leviticus, the law of the vow, offering and tithe. These are the general conditions for the sake of clarifying what goes into the surety of a vow or, rather the amount held until completion of the vow, that could be redeemed upon completion, or the case of land and other things offered to the priesthood outside of what is proscribed earlier, for the sake of a special promise to God.

It is an idea later corrupted, where we see Jesus in the Gospels call out the Pharisees for allowing an adult son to place his things in such a vow, to avoid his responsibility to honor his father and mother, caring for them in their old age, or "Corban."

*But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.*

The idea of temporarily giving or using collateral to ensure keeping of a vow before God, and redemption, is reflected in salvation, where Jesus is offered, the vow made, the Spirit serving as surety until the day of redemption.

**Hebrews 7**
*18 For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.*

*19 For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.*

*20 And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:*

*21 (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)*

*22 By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament*.

And

2 Corinthians 1
*19 For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.*

*20 For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.*

*21 Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God;*

*22 Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.*

*23 Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.*

We see these examples of promises of God are made with an application of earnest, the surety of a vow. The blood of a testimony. Redemption at the day appointed. To be paid in full as God vows. He gave His word.

This concept of contractual law is the basis of everything God does. And why He detests bearing false witness, perjury, false weights and measures, cheating and stealing...It is ultimately why salvation is by faith accepted by believing a witness testimony, the Gospel shared by a believer. Why we must be blameless, that in judgment a man may trust our confession of faith. And it is why we see the emphasis in the law of trusting multiple witnesses who testify of the same thing. It's why we have 4 Gospels.

*For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.*

And Jesus saying; *If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true. There is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true.*

The Bible is, regardless of anything else, the testimony of God to His promises, and faith is believing He is true.

God's word. Not the words of God. If that makes sense.

And we can believe His vow, that we will be redeemed, after He gave his Son as surety and the Spirit as earnest. Amen

teachings.title: The veil rent: come boldly to the throne
teachings.summary: The high priest entered behind the veil only once a year, but Christ's death rent the veil, so believers may come boldly before God at any time through Christ our high priest.
teachings.text:
Now to the narrative of events, following the deaths of Aaron's sons, God provided Aaron with an assurance that if he came before the presence of God, beyond the veil, under the ceremonial ordinances laid out; his sin offering, the linen robes and mitre that were holy, his washings, etc, that the Lord promises he will not be struck down as well. Remember, their sin was in adding to the ordinances their own doctrine, using strange fire and not the fire the Lord has provided.

And so the high priest would only enter the holy place, behind the veil, once a year to fulfill these sacrifices of atonement, first for himself and then all the people.

But when Christ had died, that veil was torn. As told by Matthew:

*And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent*...

And as Paul wrote of the veil and the unbelieving Jews:

2 Corinthians 3:14-18
*but their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away. Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.*

And so we know we may go before the Lord boldly, and at any time, because Christ is our high priest;

**Hebrews 4:14-16**
*Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession. For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

Because we have been made heirs, the sons of God and given access to the Lord by His grace and mercy, through faith in His Son;

**Ephesians 2:6**
*And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus*

For God is not slack concerning His promises.

**1 John 1:9**
 *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.*

teachings.title: Rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation
teachings.summary: Christians should be cheerful in hope, patient in trouble and constant in prayer, as Paul and Silas singing in prison won the Philippian jailer.
teachings.text:
*Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer.*

Be cheerful. Not a doomer. You have the hope of Christ, act like it. Not fearful, but let that joy come off of you. It is contagious.

Be patient in tribulation. This applies obviously to the persecution for our faith, in Christ. But it is more than that. Try not to let the petty frustrations of this world get to you, lead you to wrath, being a bad report to the Gospel we live by.

Continuing in prayer, always. Talk to God throughout the day. Give Him thanks and praise. While we shouldn't make a show of prayer, as is the habit of some, we shouldn't be ashamed to ask God's blessings for others and praise for when He answers or blesses.

Think of the Philippian Jailer, who was saved by Paul and Silas, and the church planted there that did great things for the Lord. It all came about because, despite being in chains and captive, they sang hymns and Psalms and cheerfully held themselves out as content even in tribulation.

**Philippians 2:1-5**
*If there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies, Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind. Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus*

teachings.title: The Spirit maketh intercession for us
teachings.summary: While we groan awaiting redemption, the indwelling Spirit helps our infirmities and intercedes for us according to the will of God.
teachings.text:
*For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?*
*But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.*

All of creation travailing in pain, as the pangs of birth, waiting for the day of our redemption. Not only they, but ourselves also.

There is a day to come where we will be redeemed and the Bible says that all of creation is like a woman giving birth, a new thing to be born, and that we ourselves are also in travail, having the firstfruits of the Spirit within us, that earnest expectation, sealed with that promise unto that day of redemption. This is our hope.

Hope is an earnest expectation of what is yet to come. It is the object of our faith. It isn't seen. It isn't present, it is what is to come. Having that deposit, we know we will be purchased. But we groan in ourselves waiting for that day. Stuck in the flesh.

But the Comforter, that is the Spirit of God as He resides within us, He does the will of God and works.

*Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.*

The Spirit, if we let Him, works on our infirmities, helps us with removing the thorns in our hearts that otherwise lead us to sin. He heals us as we walk in the Spirit.

But more, the Spirit is an intercessor, bringing our needs before the Father, even that which we don't know we have, that His will be done through us.

Thus we are conformed to His will, and in all things that glorify God and shape us as worthy vessels, as we walk in the Spirit and feed that new man inside.

teachings.title: Pray the Lord of the harvest for labourers
teachings.summary: Jesus commands us to pray for labourers in the harvest, so even if we do not go soul winning we must pray for those who do and to become one.
teachings.text:
*The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.*

Jesus tells us to pray that God provides laborers for the harvest. That He provide men and women willing to go forth, to the field as it were, to bring in the bounty that is ready to be picked.

If you aren't in a position to go out yourself, pray that you can be. Work towards it. But pray without ceasing for those who are, and that more may come.

Don't allow your own shortcomings, stumbling blocks and snares, perhaps embarrassment that you don't go soul winning for whatever reason (they aren't good reasons, but I am not judging. My excuses for when I don't do it are just as lame), but at least pray for those that do. Pray that God provides more who are willing to go door knocking and evangelizing. Pray you become one of them.

If Jesus tells us to pray, then pray.

teachings.title: True fasting and prayer, not to be seen of men
teachings.summary: Jesus prepared with real fasting and prayer to God, while those who deny every word of God and pray to men cannot resist temptation and fast to be seen of men.
teachings.text:
It should be mentioned that before beginning His earthly ministry, Jesus sought to purify himself with prayer and fasting. Legitimate fasting, denying Himself not personal taste and treats, preference and privilege, but actually sacrificing physical necessity that He may focus on the things of God. The word. In prayer and supplication.

How can those who deny that we have "every word of God" and that don't read it daily, allowing other men to be an intermediary, how can they resist temptation? If their prayers are to other men, not boldly going before God the Father with supplication?

They can't.

That's why they often seek worldly power. It's why they fast and pray to be seen of men, and not locked away as God commands. Not going into the wilderness but proclaiming their "sacrifice" to the world. It's why they tempt God.

teachings.title: In Every Thing Give Thanks
teachings.summary: Giving thanks in all things, good or bad, and trusting God's will will change a believer's life more than anything short of salvation.
teachings.text:
And so, a simple exercise for those of us seeking to grow in faith and understanding, by trusting in God's word and obeying His will as revealed by the same word;

**1 Thessalonians 5:18**
*In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you*

Are you thankful in all things? Do you know how to be abased, and how to abound? To trust that you can do all things through Christ, who strengthens you?

Do you have faith to **know** *that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose?*

Are you thankful for all things, good or bad, that the will of the Father for you in Christ Jesus is kept, and in so doing, regardless of what it is, good or bad, you give thanks?

This one exercise of being thankful to the Lord and trusting His will regardless of our own will, having faith that by seeking Him and following His will for us we will be blessed and rewarded, even if it isn't something we can see as yet... Even if it remains hope on His promise...This one thing will change your life as profoundly as anything short of salvation. I testify to it, God is my witness. He is not slack concerning His promises. His will be done. In all things give thanks.

teachings.title: Restoring the joy of salvation
teachings.summary: Uses Psalm 51 to encourage believers who are overcome by the world, worry and fear. Says it is fixed by turning back to God in faith and prayer, and like David singing praises and sharing the good news.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 51
**
*12 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

13 Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.

14 Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

There's many our guys who are believers, living right, and still overcome by the world. Relationships with family, being vexed by the wicked conversations of the world, work and money, inability to find a girlfriend, let alone find and keep a wife, caught up with fear and constant worry, often for good reason and rationally so, but for the joy of Jesus and the knowledge that He's overcome all, and we through Him have as well. But sometimes that fades, and the world and the old man creep in.

But it is fixed by turning towards God, in that first faith and prayer to build upon it.

And like David, sing praises unto the Lord and share with others the good news that's healed you, so it may others. Amen
